solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Outlaw assuming formal wear snubbed gangster

indicators.note: to snub originally meant to cut short, so the word loses its tail

parts.note: robing is putting on robes, formal or ceremonial dress
hood is slang for a gangster

explanation.surface: A criminal in a dinner suit cold-shoulders a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assuming formal wear' reads like a description of the outlaw, but it is one participle: robing.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the legendary English outlaw of Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Tree rising over monarch and commoner

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A tree grows above a king and a peasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commoner' looks like a noun for a non-noble, but it is the comparative adjective 'more common'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rifer is the comparative of rife, meaning more widespread, so more common.

clue.text: Old bird's uniform just the thing, overall

parts.note: a boiler is an old hen fit only for boiling
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An old bird's outfit is exactly right, all things considered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overall' seems to mean 'all in all', but it is the noun: a protective garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiler suit is a one-piece protective garment, also called an overall or overalls.

clue.text: Ignorant letters stored by one scientist

indicators.note: the letters needed are kept inside the following words, stored there

explanation.surface: A clueless scientist keeps letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescient is a literary word for lacking knowledge, from Latin nescire, not to know.

clue.text: Port city also called very backward

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the preceding letters from the end

explanation.surface: A harbour town also goes by a very old-fashioned name.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major Japanese port city on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: Fail to keep fit and initially report it's sorcery

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside
initially points to the opening letters of the next words

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone flunks a fitness test, and the first report says witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Diablerie is black magic or devilry, from French diable, devil.

clue.text: Big loss in currency conversion that Lisa avoids

indicators.note: the phrase avoids the name, so its letters are left out

explanation.surface: Someone called Lisa sidesteps heavy losses when changing money.
explanation.walkthrough: Decimalisation was Britain's switch from pounds, shillings and pence to decimal currency in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Decimation, originally killing one soldier in ten, now means heavy destruction or a large reduction.

clue.text: Every so often doubt ending of heavy responsibility

indicators.note: every so often means taking letters at intervals, skipping the ones between
the ending is just the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Now and then someone questions the end of a heavy burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is an obligation, something one is responsible for doing.

clue.text: Overthrow of government likely? That's the ticket

parts.note: as in 'the deal is on', likely to happen

explanation.surface: A coup is in the offing, and that's just what we need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the ticket' is an idiom meaning 'just right', which hides the noun ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a voucher or ticket exchangeable for goods or a discount.

clue.text: Expect it to dawn on you to underpromote pawn, we hear

definitions.text: Expect it to dawn on you

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is judged by its sound, not spelling

parts.note: in chess, underpromotion turns a pawn into a lesser piece than a queen, such as a knight

explanation.surface: A chess player realises it is wise to promote a pawn to a lesser piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Promoting a pawn to a knight rather than a queen is the classic underpromotion; 'knight' and 'night' sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a night of it is to keep celebrating late, so you expect to stay up until dawn.

clue.text: Article by children's author is set around English industrial area

indicators.note: set around means placed so as to enclose what follows

parts.note: Beatrix Potter, author of Peter Rabbit
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A children's writer's article is set in an English manufacturing district.
explanation.walkthrough: The Potteries is the Stoke-on-Trent area of Staffordshire, famous for making ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potteries is the name of the pottery-making district around Stoke-on-Trent, an industrial region.

clue.text: Zero peace with "tricky" opponents for Greek hero

parts.note: in bridge, a game of tricks, East and South are opponents

explanation.surface: Nothing, calm and wily foes add up to a hero of Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks round 'tricky' point to bridge, played in tricks, where East and South sit on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Orestes, son of Agamemnon, is the hero of Greek tragedy who avenged his father's murder.

clue.text: In pub, most of the fruit is an accompaniment to cheese

indicators.note: in means the following material goes inside the pub word
most of means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: In a pub, much of the fruit goes with the cheese board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit' and 'cheese' set a food scene, but the pub is a container split open. A Bath Oliver is a plain dry biscuit from the city of Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath Olivers are dry biscuits invented in Bath by Dr William Oliver, traditionally served with cheese.

clue.text: A fine, handsome son matters

parts.note: F for fine, as on pencil leads
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A fine, good-looking son is what counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matters' looks like a verb, but here it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Affairs are matters or business, as in 'affairs of state'.

clue.text: Some racing animal makes easy money

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit

explanation.surface: A speedy beast earns quick cash at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Buck is also American slang for a dollar, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast buck is money earned quickly and with little effort, often dubiously.

clue.text: Half a chance rugby competition fails to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the first letter is missing

explanation.surface: A rugby tournament stalls with only a fifty-fifty chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens are betting odds of one to one, a fifty per cent probability.

clue.text: Guest accommodation having run through soap, more ordered

indicators.note: something run through another passes into its middle
ordered means put into a new arrangement

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A guest room has been stocked with extra soap, as requested.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare room is a bedroom kept free for visitors, so it is accommodation for guests.

clue.text: Intrepidly having met for love, so securely sealed

indicators.note: X for Y means one thing takes the place of another

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Bravely, two lovers met in secret, sealing their bond.
explanation.walkthrough: The O in the middle of HEROICALLY is swapped out for MET.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermetically describes an airtight closure, from Hermes Trismegistus, the reputed inventor of a magic seal.

clue.text: Business's skills turned on an old group of families

parts.note: Co is company, with the S of the possessive
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: arts as in skills or crafts

explanation.surface: A firm's expertise is reshaped by a long-established set of family companies.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'X on Y' puts X after Y, so the reversed skills come after AN and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosa Nostra, Italian for 'our thing', is the Sicilian-American Mafia, organised into crime families.

clue.text: One honoured to be given sword in each hand

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces between the two hands

parts.note: L and R, left hand and right hand
given, as in 'given that', means if
an épée is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: Someone receiving an honour is presented with a sword in each hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A life peer is appointed to the House of Lords for life, with no title passing to heirs; knighting with a sword fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A life peer has been honoured with a non-hereditary peerage, sitting in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Rains hard in resort on Carroll Island

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sorted again into a new order

parts.note: Lewis Carroll, author of Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: It pours at a seaside resort on the island named after Carroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town but splits as re-sort. In an across clue 'X on Y' puts X after Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis and Harris is the largest island of the Outer Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Military exercise to capture Georgia is hotting up

indicators.note: capturing something means taking it inside

parts.note: GA is the US state abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: An army drill to seize Georgia is heating up.
explanation.definitionFit: War gaming is simulated combat used by armed forces to plan and practise operations.

clue.text: Man of principle here begins to go wrong

indicators.note: going wrong means getting mixed up and out of order

explanation.surface: A principled man starts going astray right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of principle' suggests integrity, but the principle is a scientific one.
explanation.definitionFit: Werner Heisenberg formulated the uncertainty principle in quantum mechanics.

clue.text: Revulsion from unending calamity taking time

indicators.note: taking means holding another piece inside
unending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Endless disaster that goes on and on breeds disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike or aversion, a milder form of revulsion.

clue.text: Not having committed crime, fixed then to cover a fine

indicators.note: a fixed thing has been rigged or rearranged
covering something hides it, so the new letters stand in its place

parts.note: F for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: An innocent party covers up a rigged crime and pays a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters take the place of the first F in OFFENCE. 'Not having committed' sounds like innocence, but it means undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit on the fence is to avoid committing to either side of an argument.

clue.text: Queen Victoria nursing one drink untouched

indicators.note: nursing means cradling something inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria sits nursing a drink she never touches.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin means pristine or untouched, as in virgin snow or virgin forest.

clue.text: WG Grace's first century which is one short of score?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the century Grace was born in, not his first hundred runs
second meaning: the ordinal just below twentieth, a score being twenty

explanation.surface: A cricket fan wonders about the Victorian batsman's first hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: WG Grace, Victorian England's great cricketer, lived 1848 to 1915, so 'first century' means the first century of his life, not a hundred runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace was born in the 1800s, the nineteenth century, and nineteenth comes one place before twentieth.

clue.text: French poet perceived as action hero

indicators.note: perceived here means taken in by the ear, so sound matters

parts.note: Arthur Rimbaud, the French symbolist poet

explanation.surface: A French poet is mistaken for a muscle-bound film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambo is Sylvester Stallone's commando hero in the First Blood films.

clue.text: Forced everyone at last into queue for cake

parts.note: made someone do it, forced them

indicators.note: into means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: a line of people is a queue

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter

explanation.surface: Everyone is finally pushed into a queue for cake.
explanation.walkthrough: A madeleine is the small shell-shaped French sponge cake made famous by Proust.
explanation.definitionFit: A madeleine is a small sponge cake baked in a scallop-shaped mould.

clue.text: Such sales are legal and public: what about the contrary?

parts.note: overt means open, done in public

indicators.note: about here means turned around, facing the other way

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying 'what?'
counter as in contrary or opposite

explanation.surface: Someone notes lawful open trading and asks about the opposite kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Illicit goods are sold 'under the counter', so the phrase looks like a pure riddle, but it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-the-counter sales are made openly across a shop counter, legally and without a prescription.

clue.text: Horse raced round blocks

indicators.note: something that blocks sits in the way, inside the other word

explanation.surface: A horse ran a circuit around some obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat mixes white hairs with a base colour.

clue.text: Compete in a further Scottish resort

indicators.note: in means placed inside the words that follow

parts.note: a taken as written, then more for further

explanation.surface: Take part in another contest at a Highland holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviemore is a ski and outdoor resort in the Cairngorms of the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Place for mate across the street?

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a friend or colleague

explanation.surface: Somewhere for a friend to live, just over the road?
explanation.walkthrough: Oppo is British slang for a friend or partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite means facing, on the other side, as a house across the street is.

clue.text: Did housework, lacking energy in the morning for engineering feat

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: to hoover is British for vacuuming
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone vacuumed listlessly in the morning, an impressive achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'hoover' means to vacuum, from the brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hoover Dam on the Colorado River is a celebrated feat of 1930s civil engineering.

clue.text: Preventing harm from amphibian to reporter, becoming aware back of cage is missing

indicators.note: as said to a reporter, it is the sound that counts
is missing means the letter is taken out
the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A newt is kept from harm, and a reporter notices its cage has a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The E removed is the first one in REALISING.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutralising something makes it ineffective, preventing harm from it, as with a poison or a threat.

clue.text: Nothing pub fiend knocked back is material for US serviceman

indicators.note: knocked back means read backwards, pushed the other way

explanation.surface: Nothing, a pub and a demon downing drinks make up a GI's uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers only the pub and the fiend, not the nothing at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive drab is the dull green cloth and colour of US Army uniforms.

clue.text: Deter yobs breaking up breeding ground?

indicators.note: breaking up means being broken apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Discourage hooligans from wrecking a place where trouble breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster bed is a stretch of seabed where oysters breed or are farmed.

clue.text: Fuel in fryer is provided a long way back

indicators.note: in means the following goes inside the pan word
back means read from end to start

parts.note: provided, as in 'provided that', means if

explanation.surface: Fuel in the fryer was supplied from far behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuel in fryer' looks like the definition with a place, but 'in' is the container signal and 'fryer' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is the British name for kerosene, a fuel for lamps and heaters.

clue.text: Nations combined to prevent losing king

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away

explanation.surface: An alliance of countries unites to stop a monarch being deposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of countries allied for a common purpose, such as a trading bloc.

clue.text: A few words, intelligence, by unknown military strategist

parts.note: a clause is a short group of words
z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A short message and some cleverness come from an anonymous war planner.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl von Clausewitz was the Prussian general and author of the classic treatise On War.

clue.text: Provisional ruling condemned international residence

indicators.note: condemned property is wrecked, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A temporary order condemns a foreign embassy building.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi is the court's provisional order of divorce, before the final decree absolute.

clue.text: Lying about this involves good sense

indicators.note: something lying about is turned round and back to front
involves means holds within

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Telling lies about this matter takes good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses, that of seeing.

clue.text: Perhaps stalking animal, people seized by another

indicators.note: things seized by another are held inside it

parts.note: a hart is a male deer, another animal

explanation.surface: An animal hunted by people is grabbed by another predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalking' suggests a hunting animal, but it is the crime of persistently following someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalking is a form of harassment, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Commanding speaker to enter train, overturning temporary bans

indicators.note: entering means going inside
overturning in a down clue turns the word upside down

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: A forceful spokesman boards a train that derails, leading to stoppages.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria, plural of moratorium, are temporary suspensions of an activity.

clue.text: Corks finally pulled out of wine that is sensitive to light

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'part that is sensitive to light'

indicators.note: pulled out of means removed from inside

parts.note: retsina is a resin-flavoured Greek wine

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter

explanation.surface: Corks are finally removed from wine, which spoils in daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive tissue lining the back of the eye.

clue.text: Sort of answer rest used to be

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
were, the past tense of be

explanation.surface: A kind of reply about the remainder of what once was.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were is a hedge meaning 'in a way', like 'sort of'.

clue.text: A recent criminal welcoming new admission

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in
criminal means bent, so these letters are twisted

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A recently convicted criminal welcomes a fresh arrival into prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrance means the right or act of entering, so admission, as in an entrance fee.

clue.text: Meal came up for one confined to bed?

parts.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal
rose, as the sun comes up

explanation.surface: Breakfast in bed is brought up for an invalid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confined to bed' suggests illness; the bed is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a hybrid rose grown in garden beds, a plant rooted in one place.

clue.text: Requests for soup etc all mounted up under these

definitions.meaning: first meaning: diners' orders for first courses
second meaning: jockeys on their horses await the official's word to go

explanation.surface: Diners order soup while horsemen sit ready in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: A starter is a first course, and also the official who starts a race; horses under starter's orders are about to run.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both what restaurant starters are called for and the official command riders wait under.

clue.text: Two auxiliaries fall into line

explanation.surface: Two helpers line up and conform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' and 'have' are the two main auxiliary verbs of English.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave is to act properly and conform, to fall into line.

clue.text: Make hasty escape, sued for changing gospel text

indicators.note: changing means altering the order of letters

explanation.surface: Someone flees after being taken to court over a scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatitudes are the blessings of the Sermon on the Mount in Matthew's gospel.

clue.text: Triumph in secrecy: worked out whose

indicators.note: worked out means kneaded into a new form

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whose victory was kept quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal the show is to outshine everyone else, a triumph.

clue.text: Safe places avoiding introduction of heavy plant

indicators.note: avoiding the introduction means the opening letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Refuges keep away from industrial factories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy plant' reads as industrial machinery, but plant is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Avens is a plant of the rose family, such as wood avens or mountain avens.

clue.text: Truancy in Orkney island receiving fine

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in

parts.note: Hoy is one of the Orkney islands

explanation.surface: A pupil skives off school on an Orkney isle and is fined.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoy is an island in Orkney, off the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooky, as in playing hooky, is American slang for skipping school.

clue.text: Aid to viewing French city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a piece of shaped glass in spectacles or a camera
second meaning: a town in the Pas-de-Calais

explanation.surface: A sightseeing guide to a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens focuses light to help us see, and Lens is a city in northern France.

clue.text: Very warm through day, I wrap this round?

definitions.text: Very warm through day, I wrap this round?

indicators.note: through means running into the middle of what follows

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: In the heat of the day, I wrap this garment around me.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also a picture of the garment, worn wrapped round the body in a hot climate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a loincloth worn by Hindu men, a length of cloth wrapped round the waist and legs.

clue.text: Kind of amphibian and wader almost coming to end of lake

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an egret is a wading bird

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A kind of frog and a heron arrive near the shore of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To a degree means somewhat, to some extent, like 'kind of' in casual speech.

clue.text: Regularly reads intro, just to discard when preparing text

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, every other letter

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: An editor reads introductions methodically, only to throw them away.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit out is to remove material while revising a text for publication.

clue.text: Wait to hear of weeds — not here, surely?

indicators.note: to hear means judged by the ear, so sound matters

parts.note: to queue is to wait in line
someone who weeds is gardening: he gardens

explanation.surface: Someone waits to hear about weeds, which surely cannot be here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weeds' looks like a plural noun but is a verb. Kew Gardens, the Royal Botanic Gardens in London, is surely no place for weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous botanic garden is so well tended that weeds would surely never be found there.

clue.text: European in his country perhaps left short by terribly heartless spending cuts?

indicators.note: the European is in the country, so goes inside its name
left short means cut off before the end

parts.note: an example of a European's country
E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is removed, leaving only the outside

explanation.surface: A European at home is left out of pocket by cruel government cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: AUSTRIA loses its last letter and E goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerity is a government policy of reducing public spending to cut a deficit.
